overview: This is a "resolution of inquiry," a House tool for formally asking the President to hand over documents. It asks the President to send the House, within 14 days, records about the Social Security Administration since January 20, 2025, including any access to its computer systems, which hold Social Security numbers, earnings records, and benefit payment information, by the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) or Elon Musk's team. It also asks for records on DOGE visits to Social Security offices, how the agency is carrying out several recent executive orders, daily call and visitor numbers, office closures, and staff cuts in 2025. The resolution only requests information; it does not change any policy. As of March 21, 2025, the House Ways and Means Committee had reported it unfavorably and it was placed on the House Calendar.
for: Supporters say millions of Americans depend on Social Security, so Congress should know who has accessed sensitive personal data and how staffing and office changes are affecting service.
against: Critics say the request is broad and duplicates other ways Congress can get this information, and that management of the agency is an executive branch responsibility.
